title: Standalone annotation-context framing and cross-project fidelity crosswalk
mode: Primary project issue/documentation review plus authoritative ODA and local source/test crosswalk; plan-only
scope: Review ACadSharp's standalone MLeader object-context no-op round-trip report and compare its suggested bit layout with ODA v5.4.1 §§20.4.71, 20.4.86, and 20.4.89.
Trace the local DRW_ObjectContextData parser/model, DWG object dispatch, raw callback retention, and distinction between standalone and embedded MLeader annotation-context payloads.
Cross-check recent CP949 and VERTEX-subclass peer reports against existing local generated tests, and LibreDWG's position-sensitive NOD report against local NOD-order coverage.
Refine existing PAR-20/7F.1 into a fast generated base-profile slice followed by explicit adapter-loss handling and a separate MLeader graph/consumer gate.

sources.revision: Open issue report reviewed 2026-10-19; reproduction names ACadSharp 3.7.16 and AutoCAD LT 2026; private drawings were not available or downloaded.
sources.observed: The reporter says an AC1032 no-op read/write round-trip caused AutoCAD audit errors and removal of standalone AcDbMLeaderObjectContextData objects. Two writer changes were independently reported necessary on the tested private drawings: omitting a context bit and emitting the actual leader-root count. The author says the count change may already exist on mutable master.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Version-specific peer report and native outcome; not a libdxfrw reproduction, not a current ACadSharp release qualification, and not authority for the disputed field layout.

sources.revision: Local PDF text reviewed 2026-10-19; v5.4.1. The duplicate '(1)' suffix is the actual local filename.
sources.observed: Section 20.4.89 gives the R2010 AcDbObjectContextData base sequence as common object data, BS version, B has-file-to-extension-dictionary (default true), and B default flag (default false). Section 20.4.71 adds the annotation-scale hard-pointer. Section 20.4.86 documents MLeaderAnnotContext root/line/content fields and identifies it as an annotative context helper.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Authoritative specification for the documented DWG profile. A conflicting producer stream still needs exact version/class/profile tracing; it must not silently rewrite the standard profile.

sources.revision: Shared dirty workspace inspected on 2026-10-19; no source files were modified in this pass.
sources.observed: The local context parser reads classVersion and defaultFlag without reading the intervening ODA has-file-to-extension-dictionary bit, and the model lacks a field for it. Dispatch supplies a typed shell and opaque raw frame, but the adapter retains unsupported raw objects only for EvalGraph/ACSH-history families. The embedded MLeader parser uses a separate payload route that starts at leader-root count and omits standalone base preamble/scale handle. Existing tests already cover CP949 header plus exact legacy bytes and the AC1014 base-only VERTEX subtype-marker case; generated NOD tests check position/identity rather than lowest handle.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Source/spec discrepancy and adapter route loss are confirmed by code inspection; no eligible native producer sample was used to establish consequences on a particular drawing. Existing tests were inspected but not re-run.

sources.observed: #1259 describes a CP949 header-label/body-byte mismatch and a UTF-8 fallback trap; #1279 describes a missing specific VERTEX subclass marker in AC1014; #1278 was available only as a title-level R12 POLYLINE/VERTEX duplicate-key report in this pass.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Peer issue shapes only. The first two map to already-existing local generated controls; #1278's inaccessible body supplies no normative or implementation detail.

sources.project: LibreDWG issue #1413, ezdxf ACIS docs, and FreeCAD Draft DXF docs
sources.revision: Current primary project pages reviewed 2026-10-19; no peer runtime was used.
sources.observed: LibreDWG #1413 reports object-position-dependent NOD selection and layout loss, while existing local NOD tests check owner and position. ezdxf documents limited ACIS entity parsing and inability to re-export arbitrary ACIS; FreeCAD documents its converter-to-DXF path and stock DXF import limitations for ACIS solids.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Peer-specific reports and product scope statements; not evidence of local parity or a general 3D semantic-support result.

assessment.planImpact: Refines existing PAR-20/7F.1: resolve the ODA-defined R2010+ context preamble first with generated AC1024/AC1032 field/sentinel vectors, then make opaque-object loss explicit or preserve the full owner/scale graph, and only then qualify standalone MLeader no-op round-trips at the composed native gate. Other reviewed peer shapes are matched to existing local tests and add no duplicate work.

implementationReadiness: Use the existing libdxfrw_dwg_object_vectors target and CTest registration for generated AC1024/AC1032 object frames; assert both context bits, the separate common xdictionary flag, scale handle, size boundary, and next-object sentinel with an independent test-local walker.
Treat ACadSharp #1277's suggested bit removal as a conflict lead, not a fix. If a producer-traced profile differs from ODA, name and isolate that profile and preserve the raw frame.
Before raw replay is implemented, strict conversion must expose/refuse any unretained standalone context frame without modifying the destination.
Keep standalone context object serialization separate from embedded MLeaderAnnotContext parsing and assert full handle/owner/scale/dictionary reachability before native audit.
Use touched-target build, focused selector, owning CTest, scoped diff check, and receipt validation only; keep full suite and native qualification at composed checkpoints.

method.kind: Read-only public primary-source research plus local source/test inspection and ODA specification crosswalk
method.limitations: ACadSharp #1277's input drawings are private and its suggested bit removal conflicts with ODA v5.4.1. The local mismatch is source/spec-confirmed, but producer-profile consequences are not yet established. The plan therefore requires generated spec-profile controls and a provenance-bound producer trace before adding compatibility behavior or native semantic claims.
